summary: iteration_20 — Bug regression verification for the 'black flash on objective click' bug reported by user on /ai-home. After the revert in /app/src/components/soundmap/app-shell-v5.tsx (AnimatePresence + motion.div wrapper around children removed; children now renders directly under ErrorBoundary), ALL 5 objective clicks + shell-home back-navigation transition WITHOUT any black flash. Detection method: a 20ms-tick MutationObserver-like sampler that inspected `<main>`'s computed opacity AND its firstElementChild's computed opacity throughout the 900ms following each click. In all 6 flows, mainOp stayed at 1.0 and kidOp (the page root div, 1920×4000 min-h-screen) stayed at 1.0 — i.e. no exit-fade of the outer page frame. Per-page motion.div entrance animations INSIDE each page (e.g. AI Home's whisper header initial={opacity:0}, design-hub's whisper header) still play as intended and are correctly scoped to sub-elements, not to the whole main area — this matches the reviewer's note. H1 assertions: /design shows 'Nuevo proyecto' (objective-design, no room loaded); /design?tab=optimize shows 'The Warehouse Club' (objective-optimize — expected because AIHome.onObjective calls loadDemoVenue() for any non-'design' objective, so room.name overrides the 'Nuevo proyecto' fallback in design-hub L132: `{room?.name ?? 'Nuevo proyecto'}` — this is intended and not a regression); /perform shows 'The Warehouse Club' (demo scene loaded); /analyze (SceneCompare alias) shows 'Necesitás dos escenas' (empty compare state); /analyze?tab=export same. shell-home → / lands on AI Home with data-testid='ai-home-question' visible and text '¿Qué querés hacer hoy?'. Zero real console errors observed (all HMR/wss/429 noise filtered).

regression_note: As instructed by the review, the iteration_19 'smooth cross-fade' expectation is intentionally REPLACED with 'instant navigation with per-page motion animations intact'. The removal of AnimatePresence at the shell level is correct — it was the source of the bug because RRv6 keeps `children` as a stable `<Routes>` element whose internal render depends on location, causing the exit clone to render the NEW page and fade it out. This is NOT flagged as a regression.

ai-home/index.tsx L59-65: onObjective still calls loadDemoVenue() for non-'design' objectives before navigate(obj.path). This is why /design?tab=optimize shows 'The Warehouse Club' instead of 'Nuevo proyecto' — it's an intentional UX affordance so users don't land in an empty optimize tab.

Per-page motion.div initial={opacity:0} entrance animations (design-hub L121, perform-hub L26/48/82, compare/*.tsx L153/191/212) remain scoped to sub-elements (whisper headers, cards), not to full-page wrappers — confirmed by kidOp=1 throughout every observed transition.

critical_code_review_comments: The revert is minimal and surgical — only the wrapping <AnimatePresence mode='wait'>...<motion.div key=location.pathname>...</motion.div></AnimatePresence> around `children` was removed. Per-page motion animations remain, giving users a still-lively feel without the RRv6 location-reference-hazard.
Consider adding a small unit test / vitest that asserts `<main>` never contains an AnimatePresence keyed on location.pathname, so this regression cannot silently return. Not blocking.

The onObjective auto-loadDemoVenue is helpful but has one side effect worth documenting: after clicking optimize/live/diagnose/report on a fresh install, the room state persists — so a user who then clicks 'Diseñar' (design) will see 'The Warehouse Club' pre-populated instead of the empty 'Nuevo proyecto' baseline. Not a bug in this iteration's scope, but a potential UX confusion. Currently `!hasRoom && obj.id !== 'design'` guards the auto-load correctly; the effect only fires when the user starts with no room. Acceptable behavior.

The AppShellV5 no longer wraps children in AnimatePresence — DO NOT expect shell-level cross-fade in future iterations unless intentionally re-introduced (and if so, the wrapper must NOT contain the Routes reference; e.g. use a memoized snapshot of location or lift AnimatePresence around <Routes location={location} key={location.pathname}> inside App.tsx per the RRv6 framer-motion pattern). Detection technique that worked: 20ms setInterval sampling `main` and `main.firstElementChild` computed opacity for 900ms after the click. If opacity drops < 0.05 on either, the bug has regressed. rca of the issue: iter_19 bug RCA: AppShellV5 wrapped `children` in `<AnimatePresence mode='wait'><motion.div key={location.pathname}>{children}</motion.div></AnimatePresence>`. Because React Router v6 keeps the `<Routes>` element (passed as `children`) referentially stable while its render output depends on the CURRENT `useLocation()`, the exit-cloned motion.div (still holding the same `children` reference) re-rendered the NEW page and faded it to opacity 0, then the new motion.div mounted and faded from opacity 0 up. Users perceived: new page flashes on → fades to black → fades back in. Fix (this iteration): remove the AnimatePresence + motion.div wrapper; render `{children}` directly under ErrorBoundary. Correct RRv6 + framer-motion pattern (if cross-fade is desired later) is to lift the AnimatePresence INTO App.tsx around a location-keyed `<Routes location={location} key={location.pathname}>`, so each Route's element mounts/unmounts independently with a stable identity. Verified: 6 nav flows sampled 20ms/tick for 900ms each; opacity of `<main>` and its 1920×4000 direct child stayed at 1.0 continuously. Bug is FIXED.
